signals.title: NOK/EUR — G10 Bilateral Theme + Hawkish CB Divergence
signals.text: The G10 Currency Strength Scorecard shows NOK outperforming as the weekly leader at +0.813% across 2 pairs, while EUR sits as the primary laggard at -0.571% across 9 pairs, opening a 1.384% bilateral spread. NOK/EUR strength is reinforced by Norges Bank maintaining a restrictive policy rate of 4.50% (real rate +1.82%) against the ECB at 2.65% (real rate +0.30%). NOK economic data continues to outperform with a positive ESI of +13.1, while CFTC positioning reveals EUR leveraged funds net short -82,445 contracts (6th percentile of its 52-week range). Spot EUR/NOK is severely cheap vs BEER model fair value at z=-2.16σ, but the stark policy and data divergence maintains downward pressure on EUR/NOK. Trade bias: Short EUR/NOK, exploiting the G10 bilateral divergence and carry advantage. Catalyst: Next Norges Bank rate decision on 5 Nov. Risk: EUR ESI surprises further to the upside or oil prices drop sharply, compressing the 1.384% G10 spread below 0.80%.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Hawkish FOMC Minutes + Carry Premium
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.93, holding above its SMA20 at 156.64 and SMA50 at 157.79. Fed holds at 4.00%. FX options show a strong put skew on USD/JPY with 25d RR at -1.94, indicating institutional demand for downside protection against BoJ intervention even while spot holds a yield-driven bid. USD 5Y yields have expanded +54bp over 20 days entirely led by real yields (+54bp), underscoring fundamental dollar support. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carried by positive rate differentials while holding above moving average support. Catalyst: US Initial Jobless Claims release on 8 Oct. Risk: VIX surges above 25 or Japanese authorities execute direct intervention, forcing a cover of JPY short positioning.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Extreme Positioning Squeeze + Rate Divergence
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3221, below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.3340/1.3452/1.3443. CFTC COT data shows Leveraged Funds are heavily net short GBP at -5,377 contracts, marking the 2nd percentile of its 52-week range (z=-2.34σ) with a WoW delta of -11,896 contracts. This extreme spec short positioning directly contradicts the BoE's hawkish market bias (market pricing hikes against the current 3.75% rate) and SONIA OIS support. Additionally, options market implied volatility sits elevated at IV 6.5% vs HV30 4.4% (VRP +2.0%), reflecting an active hedging premium. The combination of extreme spec shorting and hawkish rate bias creates a potent upside short-squeeze setup on any hawkish BoE catalyst. Trade bias: Long GBP/USD, positioning for a spec short squeeze back toward the 1.3340 SMA20. Catalyst: BoE Credit Conditions Survey release on 8 Oct. Risk: Sustained daily close below 1.3150 or a dovish shift in BoE pricing.

signals.title: USD/CAD — COT vs Retail Divergence + ESI Confirmation
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4255, positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.4063/1.3964/1.3860). CFTC Leveraged Funds hold net short CAD positioning at -72,519 contracts (long%=23.8%), driven by a massive +175bp Fed-BoC policy differential (Fed 4.00% vs BoC 2.25%). Retail sentiment data retail sentiment shows an extreme 96% of retail traders short USD/CAD, fading the institutional USD uptrend. This retail extreme contrasts with Canada's positive Economic Surprise Index (+15.1), suggesting that while Canadian data remains resilient, policy differentials and spec positioning dominate. Trade bias: Long USD/CAD, supported by central bank carry and institutional flow against retail exhaustion. Catalyst: Canada Employment Change release on 9 Oct. Risk: Canada jobs report beats expectations sharply, triggering a CAD rally below SMA20 support at 1.4063.

signals.title: Cross-Asset — MOVE-VIX Volatility Divergence
signals.text: The MOVE index sits at 104.4, occupying the 96th percentile of its trailing 252-session range, while the VIX index resides at 15.2, representing just the 13th percentile of its trailing year. This divergence highlights that fixed income markets are pricing significant rate path and central bank uncertainty that equity markets have yet to discount. The US 5Y yield decomposition shows a 20-day nominal move of +54bp entirely driven by real yields (+54bp real, +0bp breakeven), confirming rates market repricing. Intra-day FX market depth shows a below-average 0.73x ratio relative to the 30-day baseline, urging caution on low-volume intraday breakouts. Trade bias: Neutral FX, maintaining lower position sizing ahead of rates-driven volatility spillovers. Catalyst: Fed Governor Waller speech on 8 Oct. Risk: Fixed income volatility subsides without spilling into broader risk assets.
